title: the manifest module's doc comment says ISSUE: is retired and defends a sigil filter that no longer exists
body:
`realised_from`'s doc comment (`intentsvcs/src/intentfiles.rs`) makes two claims about the manifest, and both are false in this tree:

    /// **THE SIGIL FILTER BELOW IS A NO-OP TODAY AND IS NOT DEAD.** hv retired
    /// `ISSUE:` on 2026-08-20, so every entry is a `SteelThread` and the filter
    /// excludes nothing. It stays because the sigil space is queued to grow, and
    /// deleting it would put the bug back the day it does.

**(1) `ISSUE:` IS NOT RETIRED, AND THE LIVE MANIFEST PROVES IT.** `intent/.intentfiles` in this repository carries `ISSUE:` entries right now, one per OPEN issue, written by `organize --default`: `intentfiles.rs` filters threads on `ThreadStatus::Wip` and issues on `IssueStatus::Open` and emits both sigils, and the manifest's own header says so -- "every WIP thread and every OPEN issue is declared, and nothing else". ST0069 WP-01 gave an issue a realised form, which is what brought the sigil back, and `facade.rs` records that in the same breath as repeating the retirement claim.

**(2) THERE IS NO FILTER BELOW.** `declared_set` maps every entry through `declared_key(e.sigil, &e.id)` and excludes nothing of any kind. The filter the comment defends was removed when the set stopped being keyed on bare ids -- the history is recorded a few lines up, in `declares_thread`'s own comment about the set having been "keyed on bare ids and filtered to" threads. So the comment defends the retention of a mechanism that is already gone, and cites a test (`intentfiles_is_the_list.rs`) as recording that no fixture can catch its removal.

**WHY THIS IS WORTH A FILING RATHER THAN A QUIET EDIT.** The comment is not decoration: it states a POLICY -- that a sigil kind is retired -- in the module that owns the manifest's vocabulary, and it is the kind of sentence a reader takes as current rather than re-deriving. It was taken exactly that way on 2026-09-22 while measuring the address kinds available to `wb claim` for issue 0511: the comment reads as settling whether `ISSUE:<NNNN>` is a live address form, and the answer it gives is the wrong one. The live manifest is what corrected it.

**AND IT IS THE CLASS 0507 NAMES, IN A THIRD MECHANISM.** A statement that a mechanism is disarmed, where the mechanism is armed and nothing reports the disagreement. 0507's two instances were a shellcheck directive and an inverted `concurrency` key; this one is a doc comment, which has no checker at all, so the only thing that can catch it is a reader who doubts it.

**WHAT IS OWED.** Correct both halves against the tree: say that `ISSUE:` is live and written by `organize --default` per OPEN issue since ST0069 WP-01, and either restore the sigil filter the comment defends or delete the defence with the filter's removal recorded. Read `facade.rs`'s neighbouring copy of the same retirement claim at the same time -- one stale sentence in two homes is the shape that outlives a single-site fix.

**PROVENANCE.** Found and driven by vc on 2026-09-22 at `dd615e4b4` while establishing the design context for 0511: the six `ISSUE:` lines in the live manifest, `declared_set`'s body, and the absence of any sigil filter in the module were each read directly.


## Resolved (2026-09-22) -- one home was stale, and the second was already correct

**BOTH OF THE ISSUE'S FACTUAL CLAIMS ARE CONFIRMED, MEASURED RATHER THAN READ.** `intent/.intentfiles` carries six `ISSUE:` entries in this tree, so the sigil is live; and `declared_set` maps every entry through `declared_key` and excludes nothing, so the filter the comment defended is genuinely absent. The comment in `intentsvcs/src/intentfiles.rs` is corrected against the tree: `ISSUE:` is live, written by `organize --default` per OPEN issue since ST0069 WP-01, and the filter's removal is recorded where the defence of it used to be.

**THE SECOND HOME DID NOT NEED CHANGING, AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT.** This issue asked for `facade.rs`'s neighbouring copy to be read at the same time, on the correct principle that one stale sentence in two homes outlives a single-site fix. Read: `facade.rs:6316` says "hv retired `ISSUE:` on 2026-08-20; **ST0069 WP-01 gives an issue a realised form**, so the arm returns `issue_view`". It states the retirement as history AND its reversal in the same sentence, and then uses the reversal correctly. So the two homes had already DIVERGED -- one was updated when WP-01 landed and the other was not -- which is the ordinary way a duplicated sentence goes wrong, and is why the instruction to check both was right even though it found nothing to change.

**WHAT WAS NOT DONE AND WHY.** `facade.rs` was dirty in the shared checkout and is one of the seven files in `refs/bank/cc/0511/patch`, banked and awaiting vc's judgement. Editing it would have put an unjudged change from one node inside another node's bank -- the defect that cost dc and ic a re-cut each earlier the same day. Since the read showed nothing owed there, no coordination was needed; had it been stale, the fix would have been handed to cc rather than written here.

**THE CLASS STANDS AS FILED.** A doc comment has no checker, so the only thing that can catch it is a reader who doubts it, and the live manifest is what corrected this one.
